chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Isterabadi the Interpreter, may God be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us, on the authority of their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon him).

He said: A man came to al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! Inform me about the meaning of His Exalted and Mighty saying: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' (Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds). What is its interpretation?

He said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from al-Baqir, from Zayn al-'Abidin, from his father (peace be upon him), that a man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Inform me about the meaning of the Words of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin'. What is its interpretation?

He said: 'Al-hamdu lillahi' means that He made His servants recognize some of His blessings upon them as a whole, since they cannot recognize all of them in detail, because they are more than can be enumerated or known. So He said to them: 'Say: Praise be to Allah for what our Lord of the worlds has bestowed upon us.'

These are the groups of all created beings, from inanimate objects and animals. As for the animals, He turns them in His Power, feeds them from His sustenance, protects them under His Wing, and manages each of them according to His benefit.

As for the inanimate objects, He holds them with His Power. He keeps what is connected from falling apart, and keeps what is falling apart from coming together. He keeps the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission, and keeps the earth from sinking except by His command. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to His servants.
The Imam (peace be upon him) said: And 'Lord of the worlds' means their Owner, their Creator, and the One who directs their sustenance to them from where they know and from where they do not know.

So sustenance is divided, and it comes to the son of Adam no matter which way he goes in this world. The piety of the pious does not increase it, nor does the corruption of the wicked decrease it. There is a veil between him and his sustenance, and he is pursuing it. And if one of you were to flee from his sustenance, his sustenance would pursue him just as death pursues him.
Then Allah, the Majestic, said: 'Say: Praise be to Allah for what He has bestowed upon us and mentioned us with as good in the books of the ancients before we existed.'

In this is an obligation upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and upon their followers to thank Him for what He has favored them with. This is because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, sent Moses, son of Imran, and chose him as a confidant, and split the sea for him, and saved the Children of Israel, and gave him the Torah and the Tablets, he saw his rank near his Lord, the Exalted and Mighty.

He said: O Lord! You have honored me with an honor that You have not honored anyone before me with. Then Allah, the Majestic, said: O Moses! Do you not know that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is superior to Me in the sight of all My angels and all My creation?
Moses said: O Lord! If Muhammad is more honored with You than all Your creation, is there among the Households of the Prophets one more honored than my household?
Then Allah, the Majestic, said: O Moses! Do you not know that the virtue of the Family of Muhammad over all the Households of the Prophets is like the virtue of Muhammad over all the Messengers?

Moses said: O Lord! If the Family of Muhammad is like that, is there among the nations of the Prophets one more superior to You than my nation, for whom You shaded with clouds, sent down Manna and Quail, and split the sea?
Then Allah, the Majestic, said: O Moses! Do you not know that the virtue of the nation of Muhammad over all the nations is like his virtue over all My creation?

Moses said: O Lord! I wish I could see them. Then Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, revealed to him: O Moses! Indeed, you will not see them, for this is not the time of their appearance. But you will see them in the Gardens, the Gardens of Eternity and Paradise, in the presence of Muhammad, where they will move about in its bliss and wallow in its goodness.

Do you like for Me to let you hear their speech? He said: Yes, my God. Allah, the Majestic, said: Stand before Me and tighten your girdle, the standing of a humble servant before the Majestic King. So Moses (peace be upon him) did that.

Then our Lord, the Exalted and Mighty, called out: O nation of Muhammad! And they all answered Him while they were in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers: 'Here I am, O God, here I am. No partner for You, here I am. Indeed, praise and grace are Yours and the Kingdom. No partner for You.'

He said: So Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, made that response the slogan of Hajj. Then our Lord, the Exalted and Mighty, called out: O nation of Muhammad! Indeed, My Mercy has preceded My Wrath, and My Forgiveness before My Punishment.

So I have answered you before you call Me, and I have given you before you ask Me. Whoever meets Me from you with the testimony that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, truthful in his words and right in his actions, and that Ali ibn Abi Talib is his brother and his successor after him and his guardian, and he commits to obeying him as he commits to obeying Muhammad.

And that his chosen, purified, and distinct guardians, who are distinguished by the wonders of Allah's signs and the proofs of Allah's arguments, after the two of them, are His guardians. I will admit him to My Paradise, even if his sins are like the foam of the sea.

He said: So when Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, sent our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), He said: O Muhammad! And I was not at the side of Tur when I called your nation with this honor. Then He, the Exalted and Mighty, said to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): Say: 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds' for what He has singled me out for with this virtue.
And He said to his nation: 'Say: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds' for what He has singled us out for with these virtues.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤَمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the interpretation of 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' by defining praise as acknowledging God's general blessings on all creation, while linking this verse to the specific privilege of the Prophet's family. The narration employs a theological dialogue with Moses to establish the pre-existence and supreme status of the Ummah of Muhammad, framing the call 'Labbayk' as a primordial affirmation of their divine election and eventual entry into Paradise.
